_comment: Auto-pairing rules for the parity gate. Data, not code: adding a rule is a
reviewable line here rather than a patch to check-parity.mjs.
EVERY RULE IS ADDITIVE. A rule adds a name an id may claim; it never
replaces the name as written. Replacing is destructive and the real
surface proved it: `_path` is a declared overload suffix so `fill_path`
reaches `fill`, and stripping it unconditionally also ate `close_path`
into `close` and `begin_path` into `begin`.
WHAT ADDITIVITY COSTS, FOR ANYONE MEASURING A PROPOSED ALIAS. Adding
names can only add pairings, so the pairs an alias LOSES is now
structurally zero -- for every alias, always. A harness reporting gained,
lost and collisions therefore has a column that cannot move, sitting
where a reader expects a measurement, and a control chosen because it
loses pairings no longer demonstrates the harness can see a cost.
RANK BY GAIN MINUS COLLISIONS, OR REPORT BOTH COLUMNS. A proposal with a
higher gain and a worse collision count is not the better candidate, and
an instrument that ranks on overlap alone will say it is. Measured:
`WindowSpec -> Window` gains 14 and collides 17 times; `WindowSpec ->
WindowOptions` gains 13 and collides not at all. Overlap alone prefers the
first, which is how it came to be proposed, refused at 43 collisions, and
replaced by an entry -- against the wrong npm holder the whole time.
That is the same failure as the LOST column above, from the other end: one
column has stopped discriminating, the other was never consulted.
What still discriminates is the collision count, and whether the gain is
of members that MEAN something. `TextEngine -> ParagraphBuilder` gains
two ids and collides with nothing, and the two are `new` meeting `new` --
a name every class on both surfaces carries. No arithmetic separates that
from a real pairing, so a measurement is not sufficient to accept an
alias and the evidence line has to say what the shared members are.
THE DUPLICATE THAT PARALLEL EDITING PRODUCES, in case you are about to
make it. Eight instances so far, and every one is the same shape: a live
entry names a holder's members and misses the bare holder id, so the next
person to meet that holder writes an entry for it -- correct, not
redundant, no merge conflict, and nothing but a check comparing ids will
say the two overlap.
The fix is always one appended line rather than a competing entry: add
the bare id to the entry that already names its members. `Projection`,
`DashPattern` and `PaintStyle` all went that way. If you are adding a
holder's members, add the holder.
AN ALIAS NAMING SOMETHING NO EXTRACTOR PRODUCED FAILS AS `stale`, exactly
as a manifest entry does. An exception list is where a real gap goes to be
silenced: of twelve member-level 'naming exceptions' proposed for this
file, zero were naming problems. Four were capability gaps -- `Affine` has
no skew of any kind against six npm members -- and an alias would have
reported agreement on members that do not exist, in the one layer no
extractor guard can see.
_owner_aliases: Only holders whose NAME differs across the surfaces. The mixin split is
not here: it is derived from the npm payload's `heritage`, so a new mixin
needs no edit and cannot be forgotten.
_owner_aliases_is_empty_on_purpose: The seven `js_names` re-exports are DERIVED from the extractor payload --
`src/lib.rs` declares them and says `Every item here is a re-export, not a
new type`. A hand-written line here would be a line someone can forget,
and forgetting it makes a silently unmapped holder. This is for a rename
the crate does NOT declare; a hand entry still overrides a derived one.

_owner_aliases_evidence._what: Each line is a member-by-member comparison against the real payload, not a name that looked plausible. Rust matched / Rust total, and what did not match. Re-derived here against target/parity-*.json rather than carried over from the population pass, whose figures came from a parse of lib/index.d.ts before the extractor emitted union members.
_owner_aliases_evidence.Cursor -> CursorStyle: 34/36. The residue is `ALL` and `as_css`, a variant and a helper, not absences.
_owner_aliases_evidence.FontStretch -> CanvasFontStretch: 9/9. npm also declares FontWidthName with the same nine; CanvasFontStretch is the one the context property uses, so FontWidthName is a second npm name for one Rust type and is a manifest entry rather than a second alias.
_owner_aliases_evidence.ImageFormat -> ExportFormat: 12/19; the seven are helper methods, registered as a capability.
_owner_aliases_evidence.PixelColorSpace -> ColorSpace: 8/9, the residue being `as_str`. npm has 15 because it carries an alias for every space.
_owner_aliases_evidence.PixelDepth -> ColorType: 10/24 by name alone; the rest are acronym spellings reached by member aliases below. npm has 26.
_owner_aliases_evidence.TextDirection -> CanvasDirection: 1/3 by spelling; ltr and rtl are member aliases. Three states each, paired by meaning, which is what an alias is for.
_owner_aliases_evidence.TextureOptions -> CreateTextureOptions: 7/8. `spacing` is reachable as a positional parameter and is registered.
_owner_aliases_evidence.StrutStyle -> StrutStyleInput: 4/6 direct, the other two by member alias.
_owner_aliases_evidence.TextShadow -> TextShadowInput: 1/4 direct; the rest by member alias, including a documented sigma-to-radius conversion.
_owner_aliases_evidence._WindowSpec -> Window is REFUSED: Proposed at 14/16 and measured at 43 collisions, every one of them this alias. Rust already has its own `Window` holder declaring the same members, so the alias makes two unrelated Rust holders claim one npm name -- `Window::background` and `WindowSpec.background` both reach `Window.background`. That is the same shape as the EngineDetails refusal, mirrored: there two npm holders would have claimed one Rust holder. `Window` is the live window and `WindowSpec` its construction options; two capabilities, one npm spelling, so it is a manifest entry.
_owner_aliases_evidence.TextStyle -> TextStyleInput: 18/28. TextStyle also feeds npm's ParagraphStyleInput, which an alias cannot express -- see the manifest.
_owner_aliases_evidence.EncodeOptions -> ExportOptions: 8/16 direct, 11 with the three member aliases. The rest reach RenderOptions and ImageDataExportSettings, which an alias cannot express -- see the manifest.
_owner_aliases_evidence._rejected: TextSlant -> FontSlantName and EngineDetails -> BackendInfo are both refused and must stay refused: in each case the npm target already has a Rust claimant, and a second alias onto it would let a gap in either hide behind the other.

_overload_suffixes: `_radians` and `_degrees` are the unit pair: two spellings of one
operation, so `skew_x_radians` and `skew_x_degrees` both reach npm's one
`skewX`. Eight Rust members carry them, all on `Affine`; the six skew
ones land on real npm members and `rotation` correctly reaches nothing,
since npm spells that `rotate` and it is registered as a capability.
_strip_suffixes: A trailing `Sync` on the npm side. `_sync` appears nowhere in the 1371
Rust ids -- the crate is synchronous, and npm carries the pair only
because JavaScript has an event loop to get off. One line lands on three
real pairs and correctly reaches nothing for the other three, which are
capability questions rather than spelling ones.
_make_prefix_holders: npm spells these `Make` + PascalCase of the Rust name. Scoped to the four
holders that do it rather than applied everywhere, so it cannot invent a
pairing on a holder with no such convention. 35 npm members against Rust
`Shader` DOES FIRE, and a review reported that it could not. It was right
about the tree it read: the rule matches on the holder name AFTER
aliasing, and while owner aliases REPLACED the written name, Rust
`Shader` only ever reached `spellings` as `CanvasGradient` -- so the
entry matched nothing. Owner aliases add rather than replace now, so the
holder arrives under both names and the entry pairs
those four ids; that is measured, not assumed.
_acronyms: Runs of capitals that mechanical camelCase gets wrong: `to_data_url`
becomes `toDataUrl` where npm writes `toDataURL`. Four settle every case
in the surface, one of them inside the `Make` family.
_acronyms_are_longest_first: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Each acronym is applied by replacing its Titled
form, so a shorter one that is a prefix of a longer one fires first and
eats it: with `SRGB` ahead of `SRGBA`, `Srgba8888` becomes `SRGBa8888`,
which matches nothing. That is not hypothetical -- it is what the gate
reported for `ColorType.SRGBA8888` before `SRGBA` was added ahead of it.
Keep this list sorted longest first, and check a new entry against every
existing one it is a prefix of.
_string_literals_are_values_not_names: A string literal reachable under two npm union types is NOT a collision,
and a check that reported one would be correct and useless. Measured from
the TypeScript AST of lib/index.d.ts:
51  distinct literals claimed by more than one type
19  type PAIRS sharing at least one literal
5  pairs sharing at least two
3  pairs sharing at least five
15  types involved
Three readers agree on those, independently. An earlier note here said
`eleven type pairs`; eleven is the number of distinct co-occurrence SETS
-- `destination` sits in three types and is one set but three pairs, and
`normal` sits in five and is one set but ten. Right about a different
quantity, and the label was what made it unverifiable.
The largest groups are `BlendMode` with `CanvasCompositeOperation`, then
the two font-stretch types and the two font-variant types. The three the
divergence names -- clear, destination, modulate -- are one pair of the
nineteen.
The three named in AGENTS.md are the documented divergence --
`globalCompositeOperation` takes `clear`, `destination` and `modulate`,
which the standard does not list, and `CompositeExtension` exists as its
own type so a caller knows which half they are using. They are
deliberately reachable as blend modes AND as composite operations. So is
most of the rest: `source-over` is a blend mode and a composite operation
because it genuinely is both.
WHY NO CHECK IS NEEDED FOR THIS. Ids are holder-qualified, so
`BlendMode.clear` and `CompositeExtension.clear` are already two ids with
two names, and nothing pairs them. The hazard is not the shared literal;
it is a PAIRING that names the wrong holder, which is how
`BlendMode::Copy` came to be matched against a `GlobalCompositeOperation`
spelling. That is a review question about one manifest entry, not a
property of the vocabulary, and no mechanical check over literals can see
it -- both halves of a mis-targeted pairing look correct locally.
`GlobalCompositeOperation = CanvasCompositeOperation | CompositeExtension`
is a union OF the other two. If union members ever get ids, that relation
is the string-side analogue of `heritage` and should be derived the same
way, so a literal declared in a component claims the union's name too.
_member_aliases: Keyed `Holder.member` first, bare member name second, and ADDITIVE --
the alias adds a spelling rather than replacing the derived ones.
A bare key is global and a member name is not. `height` is declared on
sixteen Rust holders, so `StrutStyle.height -> heightMultiplier` written
bare would also rewrite `Canvas.height`, `Image.height` and `Rect.height`.
`F16` and `F32` are `PixelDepth` variants and also function keys on `Key`.
Seven of the twenty aliases proposed by the population pass collide that
way, which is why the key carries the holder.
MANY-TO-ONE IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE and is refused by measurement, not
by taste: two keys mapping to one npm member make both ids claim that
name and the collision check stops the run. Four proposals have hit it --
TextShadow's two offsets, FontLibrary's two register calls, Canvas's
`new_page_with` beside `new_page`, and Window's `set_cursor_css` beside
`set_cursor`. All four are capability entries instead. A reader and its
setter are the exception, excused by name, so `App.mode` and
`App.set_mode` may both claim `eventLoop`.
`TextShadow.offset_x` and `offset_y` are NOT here. npm carries one
`offset` member for the pair, so aliasing both makes them claim one name
and the collision check refuses it -- correctly, since an alias asserts
one capability spelled two ways and this is two Rust members answering
one npm one. It is a manifest entry.
